ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA/GwG), SR 955.0 (of 10 October 1997, consolidated as of 1 January 2024), notably Art. 4 (identification of beneficial owner) and Art. 6 (enhanced due diligence on politically exposed persons); Swiss Code of Obligations (CO/OR), SR 220, Arts. 626–763 (Aktiengesellschaft), Arts. 697i–697m (register of bearer shareholders) and Art. 51 (registered seat in Switzerland); Swiss Criminal Code Arts. 305bis and 305ter (money laundering and lack of financial diligence); Federal Act on the Commercial Register and Commercial Register Ordinance (HRegV), SR 221.411; FINMA Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance (AMLO-FINMA), SR 955.033.2; Money Laundering Ordinance (VwGw), SR 955.01. Switzerland operates no public UBO register; beneficial-ownership disclosure is effected through AMLA-regulated financial intermediaries, the internal share register, and lawful governmental access only.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all applicants, directors, shareholders and UBOs against the SECO consolidated Swiss/UN/EU sanctions list (SR 946.231.1 and SECO embargoes), the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the United States OFAC SDN List (mandatory due to USD clearing and Etsy/Stripe USD exposure), the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List and, where applicable, the UK OFSI Consolidated List. PEP negative-media, beneficial-ownership and source-of-wealth checks are mandatory under AMLA Art. 6 for foreign and domestic politically exposed persons, their family members and close associates, requiring senior-management approval, documented source of funds and ongoing transaction monitoring for the life of the banking and merchant relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix – Central Business Name Index (Zentraler Firmenindex), operated by the Federal Commercial Register Office (EHRA/FFGC) of the Federal Department of Justice and Police, integrated with the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB/SOGC) and cantonal commercial register offices (Handelsregisterämter); name reservations are filed electronically through the cantonal registry using the e-register/eGRIS channel
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: CO Art. 944 requires the firm name to be written in Latin characters; non-Latin script (e.g., Chinese characters) is not registrable as a company name and may appear only as an unofficial trading style or product mark outside the registered firm. The primary firm name must be comprehensible in one of the Swiss national languages (German, French, Italian or Romansh) and must include the legal-form suffix 'Aktiengesellschaft' or 'AG' (German) or the equivalent 'Société Anonyme' / 'SA' (French or Italian usage). A secondary foreign-language trading name may be registered as an ancillary business designation (HRegV Art. 19) but must accompany a compliant primary name. Transliteration of foreign shareholder names on corporate documents must be rendered in the Latin alphabet with exact identity matching against UBO passports.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank / Bankier / Sparkasse (banking supervision prior authorization required)
Insurance / Versicherung / Assurance (FINMA insurance authorization required)
Trust / Trust Company / Treuhandgesellschaft (FINMA licensing under Financial Institutions Act where trust/asset-management activity is implied)

Swiss / Schweiz / Suisse / Svizzera / Helvetia / Helvétique and the Swiss cross (Swissness Act: permitted only where the company meets the Swissness value-added and seat control thresholds under CO Art. 929 and Trade Mark Protection Act Art. 47, i.e., at least 50% Swiss manufacturing cost share for industrial goods)
Federal / Eidgenössisch / Confédéral / National / Staats- (terms falsely implying state affiliation)
Coop / Migros / Protekta (protected private marks and public-order denominations)
Stiftung / Fondation (foundation form) and any term implying charitable, religious or public-interest purpose contrary to AG commercial status
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The applicant receives a written ruling from the competent cantonal commercial register office stating the legal grounds for rejection. The applicant may (1) submit a written amendment or rebuttal to the same registry office within 10 days of the negative ruling; (2) lodge a formal administrative appeal with the cantonal supervisory authority for the commercial register (Handelsregisteraufsichtsbehörde) within 30 days of the ruling; and (3) seek final recourse before the Federal Administrative Court (Bundesverwaltungsgericht, St. Gallen) against the cantonal supervisory decision. A rejected name may be resubmitted after cure of the grounds of refusal; no statutory extension of the initial 90-day reservation exists, and re-filed reservations are reprocessed with fresh priority.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A bare virtual mailbox without physical accessibility is not permitted as a statutory registered seat under CO Art. 51 and HRegV. The AG must maintain a physical administrative seat in Switzerland where the board minutes, share register, statutory records and accounting books are effectively kept. Commercial domiciliation (Sitzdomizil / fiduciaire de domiciliation) operated by a licensed fiduciary is accepted in Canton Zug and Zürich only where the provider maintains a physical reception, dedicated client files and demonstrable administrative substance; for an ISIC 3240 manufacturing entity with Etsy and Stripe merchant rails, a residential home address with landlord consent and actual administrative activity remains the minimum viable alternative, and a pure virtual office will be refused by the commercial register and by banking/money-laundering compliance review.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified at 5% to 10% probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection within the first 24 months of operations for a Low_Risk_Standard manufacturing entity; the majority of examinations are desk audits by the cantonal tax administration or the AHV/Social Insurance compensation office rather than commercial-register site visits; the likelihood increases materially above 15% where the registered seat is a domiciliation mailbox lacking evidence of genuine administrative activity.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cantonal notarial fee schedule; CHF 1,200–2,500 depending on nominal capital and canton (Zug benchmark approximately CHF 1,500)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial register entry fee for AG incorporation

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR / Code des obligations), Arts. 620-763 (Aktiengesellschaft), in particular Art. 621 (minimum capital), Art. 622 (share categories), Art. 629 (registration application), Arts. 632-633 (pay-up and bank confirmation), Art. 640 (entry in the Commercial Register), Art. 716a (non-transferable board powers); complemented by the Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV) of 17 October 2007, SR 221.411.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Office du registre du commerce) of the corporate seat canton, filing via the federal electronic transmission (TERE) by a notary; federal supervision by the Federal Office of Justice (Bundesamt für Justiz, BJ); publication through the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB/SOGC).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarially certified Articles of Association (Statuten) and registration application (Anmeldung zur Eintragung ins Handelsregister) under Art. 640 OR, together with the capital-liberation bank certificate, the list of directors and signatories, and declarations required by HRegV Arts. 20-23.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Nominal share capital must be at least CHF 100,000 and paid up to at least 20% of the par value of each share, with an aggregate minimum of CHF 50,000 (Arts. 621 and 632 OR). Payments must be deposited in a Swiss bank and be freely disposable by the company before registration, evidenced by a bank liberation/confirmation certificate under Art. 633 OR (blocked account 'Sperrkonto' is customary).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] AG: (1) The founders' share subscription statements in the notarized deed are ratified; the paid-up capital of at least CHF 50,000 is deposited in a Swiss bank and is freely disposable, per bank liberation certificate. (2) The registered office is established at [street, zip, city], Switzerland, and publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB) is ordered. (3) The following persons are appointed as directors for the first term, each signing individually: [name, date of birth, nationality, address]. (4) All filings, including commercial register, social insurance and tax registrations, are approved. The resolution is immediately effective.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name clearance and pre-incorporation document preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Business Name Index (Zentraler Firmenindex, www.zefix.ch) and the civil-law notary public (Notariat) of the seat canton
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search on Zefix and verify the proposed name is true, clear, not misleading and clearly distinguishable under Art. 950 OR. Instruct the notary to draft the Articles of Association (Statuten), share subscription form, and the public deed text, and to request a preliminary name reservation. Collect certified passport copies and specimen signatures of all founders and intended directors.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name (three alternatives)
Draft Articles of Association (Statuten)
Certified passport or ID copies of founders and intenden board members
Zefix name search printout
Notarized power of attorney if a founder acts by representation
Short curriculum vitae of each founder (for bank and due diligence)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Register rejects the name as confusing or misleading, resubmit a corrected alternative name with written justification, or apply for an administrative exemption; the notary coordinates any amended deed wording without restarting the process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of notarial incorporation deed and appointment of corporate organs
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Civil-law notary public (Notariat / Notaire) with certification power in the seat canton
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold a notarial session where all founders or their authorized representatives subscribe the shares, adopt the Articles of Association and give their irrevocable subscription declarations. The notary records in the deed the appointment of the Board of Directors and the election or waiver of an audit company in accordance with the 'opting-out' rules (Art. 727a OR). Signatures and specimen signatures are certified, and the instrument is dated and sealed.
required_dossiers: Final signed Articles of Association
Share subscription and pay-up declaration signed by founders
Acceptance statements of Board members
Auditor acceptance statement only if ordinary audit is not waived
Identity documents and official signature specimens of directors
Founders' resolution on in-kind contributions (if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies legal defects (e.g., under-capitalization, inaccurate share provisions), execute a corrective notarial addendum before filing; if the employees' election threshold is met, supplement the deed with the employee representative documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of paid-up capital and issuance of Swiss bank liberation certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Swiss bank duly recognized by the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the bank to open a blocked corporate account (Sperrkonto) in the name of the company under formation. Pay in at least CHF 50,000 (or the higher amount fixed by the Articles) from the founders. The bank verifies sources of funds and issues an Art. 633 OR capital-liberation certificate confirming that the capital is paid and at the free disposal of the company's board. The funds are released to the operating account upon Commercial Register entry.
required_dossiers: Swiss bank account opening forms for the company under formation
Draft Articles of Association and founders' KYC information
Payment order or SWIFT confirmation evidencing CHF 50,000 deposit
Board directors' specimen signatures for the bank
Undertaking to provide final registration excerpt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further anti-money-laundering documentation (source of funds, beneficiary ownership), submit the notarial deed and audited bank statements; alternatively replace the bank and issue a new liberation certificate at no additional registry cost.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of registration application to the Cantonal Commercial Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Office du registre du commerce) of the seat canton, lodged electronically by the notary via the TERE platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Transmit to the Commercial Register the notarized incorporation deed, bank liberation certificate, the official registration application form (Form 44), and the statutory declarations regarding enforcement proceedings, bankruptcy risk and social-security arrears of the company and its directors. The Registry verifies compliance with Art. 640 OR and HRegV, allocates the enterprise identification number (UID), and issues the registration excerpt and definitive company name entry in Zefix.
required_dossiers: Notarized public deed of incorporation
Swiss bank capital-liberation certificate (Art. 633 OR)
Commercial Register application form (Form 44)
Declaration on pending enforcement or bankruptcy proceedings
Certification of no AHV (social security) contribution arrears
Consent of the owner for use of the registered office address
Authenticated signature card of each director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to the Registry's request for supplementary information (Mängelrüge / complément) within the statutory deadline, usually 10 working days, by submitting the missing document or a corrective notarial deed; an adverse final refusal may be appealed to the cantonal commercial register supervisory authority within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration publication in SHAB and tax-social security coordination
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB/SOGC), Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA), and the cantonal AHV compensation fund (Ausgleichskasse)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon registration the Cantonal Commercial Register issues the entry and the SHAB publication occurs automatically. Thereafter, assess VAT registration duty (annual turnover threshold CHF 100,000; Art. 10 VAT Act; voluntary registration permitted) and file the VAT registration with the FTA where required. Register the employer with the statutory AHV/IV/EO compensation fund, obtain the employer number, and conclude compulsory accident insurance with SUVA for all employees. Archive all excerpts and confirmations in the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register excerpt after entry (Zefix printout)
VAT registration questionnaire (Abklärung der Steuerpflicht)
Employer registration form for the AHV compensation fund
SUVA employer accident-insurance declaration
SHAB publication certificate
Company seal and signature cards (final)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the FTA or the AHV compensation fund raises queries about the effective commencement date or projected turnover, file a signed clarification statement with the requested supporting accounts; counsel liaises to expedite issuance of the definitive VAT number and social insurance employer number.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Cantonal building and industrial licensing office (Baubewilligungsbehörde / Amt für Gewerbe und Arbeit) of the seat canton, in coordination with the municipal building department and the cantonal environmental office (Amt für Umwelt)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Industrial operating permit and premises use authorization (Betriebsbewilligung für Gewerberäume) under cantonal building law, including the mandatory building and use permit for the production workshop and the waste-water discharge/exhaust-air permits required by the cantonal environment authority.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (BAFU/FOEN) together with the cantonal environmental protection office (Amt für Umwelt / Dienststelle Umwelt) of the seat canton
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C - Registration/notification tier (Vorprüfung/Anmeldestufe) under the Swiss EIA Ordinance (UVP-Verordnung of 19 October 1988, SR 814.011). No full EIA report is required for a micro-scale enamel-pin polishing and surface-finishing workshop, provided electro-polishing bath capacity is below 2,000 litres and annual wastewater discharge is below 500 m³; a formal classification decision (Feststellungsverfügung) will be obtained.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: compliance with the Swiss Waters Protection Ordinance (Gewässerschutzverordnung, GSchV, SR 814.201), Appendices 2 and 3 - maximum pollutant loads for sewer discharge: total suspended solids ≤ 20 mg/L, COD ≤ 60 mg/L, copper ≤ 0.5 mg/L, nickel ≤ 0.5 mg/L, zinc ≤ 2 mg/L, lead ≤ 0.3 mg/L; pH 6.5-9.0; neutralization and precipitation tank required before sewer connection. Air emissions: compliance with the Clean Air Ordinance (Luftreinhalte-Verordnung, LRV, SR 814.318.142.1) - volatile organic compounds (VOCs) from enamel-drying ovens ≤ 20 mg/m³ total carbon, particulate matter ≤ 20 mg/m³, with emissions captured by a wet scrubber and a certified filter system. Waste: metal sludge and enamel residue must be disposed of at an authorized facility pursuant to the Waste Ordinance (VVEA, SR 814.600).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety clearance issued by the cantonal fire prevention authority (Feuerpolizei / VKF) evidencing compliance with fire-protection classifications and escape routes for the production workshop; structural and load inspections confirmed by the cantonal building inspectorate for machinery placement; occupational workplace clearance from the cantonal labor inspectorate (Arbeitsinspektorat) under Art. 82-84 of the Swiss Labour Act (Arbeitsgesetz, SR 822.11), including noise protection and fume-exhaust verification; compulsory occupational and non-occupational accident insurance contract with SUVA (UVG, SR 832.20), first-aid provision, and workstation certificates.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC), Berne, via the official portal www.estv.admin.ch and ePortal; cantonal profit and capital taxes are administered by the Zug Canton Tax Office (Kantonales Steueramt Zug).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the CH_AG in the Zug Commercial Register (Handelsregister) with minimum share capital of CHF 100,000 (at least CHF 50,000 paid in); the Swiss Federal Statistical Office then automatically issues the UID business identification number (9-digit CHE-xxx.xxx.xxx). Step 2: Apply for VAT registration with the ESTV once worldwide turnover from taxable supplies reaches CHF 250,000 per annum (Art. 10 VAT Act; threshold as of 1 Jan 2025; previously CHF 100,000; voluntary registration is permissible below the threshold). Step 3: Submit the ESTV registration form and factual sheet declaring the ISIC 3240 business activity (die-struck brass enamel pin manufacture and merchandising), expected turnover by market, and the choice between effective input-tax method and flat-rate method. Step 4: Receive the Swiss VAT number in the form of the UID with the suffix MWST/TVA, e.g., CHE-xxx.xxx.xxx MWST, and obtain separate cantonal direct-tax numbers from the Zug tax authority for federal, cantonal and communal income/capital tax returns. Step 5: Because the CH_AG is Swiss-resident, no fiscal representative is required, unlike foreign e-commerce sellers without a Swiss establishment who use the simplified ESTV registration procedure.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - the Aktiengesellschaft is a non-transparent legal entity taxed at the federal, cantonal and municipal levels; federal statutory corporate income tax is 8.5% (approximately 7.83% effective after deduction of federal tax), Zug combined effective profit tax is approximately 11.9%, and Zug capital tax is approximately 0.04%-0.05% on taxable equity; no US-style check-the-box or general pass-through election exists; shareholder distributions are subject to Swiss withholding tax of 35% unless paid from qualifying capital contribution reserves properly tracked in a separate reserve account.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Available elections: (1) VAT flat-rate method (Saldosteuersatz) election under Art. 34 VAT Act for Swiss businesses with turnover up to approximately CHF 5 million, simplifying export refund substantiation; (2) Art. 11 VAT Act option to waive the small-business exemption and register voluntarily for VAT; (3) STAF 2020 tax reform elections at cantonal level, including the patent-box deduction (relief up to 90% of qualifying IP income) and the notional interest deduction on excess equity; (4) Swiss Merger Act election to preserve the capital contribution reserve account at book value so that returns of paid-in capital can be made free of 35% Swiss withholding tax; (5) VAT grouping election under Art. 20 VAT Act for related Swiss companies, not relevant for a standalone AG; Switzerland provides no hybrid mismatch or check-the-box election, and the Swiss AG is always a separate corporate taxpayer.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT / Mehrwertsteuer MWST / TVA) under the Swiss Federal Act on Value Added Tax of 12 June 2009 (VAT Act, SR 641.20), administered by the ESTV/AFC using the UID with MWST/TVA suffix.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 250,000 annual worldwide turnover from taxable supplies (Art. 10 VAT Act as amended from 1 Jan 2025; previous threshold CHF 100,000). The Swiss-resident CH_AG must register mandatorily when this worldwide threshold is exceeded; below it, VAT registration is optional. A foreign seller without a Swiss establishment is generally required to register only for Swiss-sourced supplies not benefiting from the B2B reverse charge; the CH_AG is Swiss-resident and therefore applies the CHF 250,000 domestic threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland has no real-time fiscal clearance system, no continuous transaction control (CTC), no digital stamping, and no state gateway API for invoice pre-clearance; e-invoicing is voluntary in the B2B/B2C segment but standardised through the eBill/Peppol network and becomes mandatory for suppliers invoicing the Swiss Federal Administration (B2G) in 2026; every VAT invoice must meet Art. 26 VAT Act content requirements (supplier name/address/UID, recipient name/address, date, description of goods, consideration, VAT rate and VAT amount, and for exports the statement of 0% VAT); the Swiss QR-bill with QR-IBAN is the standard payment-invoice format for Swiss payers; Etsy Direct Pay and Stripe settlement records must be preserved as auxiliary evidence of export sales.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% export VAT rate applies under Art. 23(2) VAT Act where hard enamel lapel pins are physically exported by the CH_AG or by a third party on its behalf, title and risk pass to the foreign customer abroad, and the goods leave the Swiss customs territory and remain abroad; the export evidence must be in the records when the VAT return is filed. Services directly connected to export goods, including die-struck brass processing, cloisonné enamelling and polishing work performed on movable goods for a foreign principal, are equally zero-rated if the processed goods are subsequently exported. For Etsy/Stripe cross-border sales, zero-rating is substantiated by despatch abroad via Swiss Post, DHL or FedEx with CN22/CN23 customs declarations, the foreign shipping address and the marketplace/bank settlement showing the non-Swiss buyer; supplies delivered to a Swiss address remain taxable at the standard 8.1% rate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Swiss Customs Export Declaration (electronic exit summary via the Swiss customs platform or postal CN22/CN23 customs declaration attached to the consignment as formal export evidence)

Bill of Lading (sea freight), Air Waybill (air freight) or postal/courier consignment note with tracking (Swiss Post, DHL, FedEx) evidencing despatch from Switzerland and delivery to the foreign destination

Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent settlement proof, being Etsy Direct Pay and Stripe payout statements, foreign-currency SWIFT/SEPA credit advices and the foreign buyer's payment and shipping details
Commercial invoice expressly stating 'Export - VAT 0%' and including the ISIC 3240 product description, quantity, unit price, Incoterms and destination country
Carrier confirmation or delivery receipt showing physical exit of the goods from Swiss customs territory
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ESTV may review export zero-rating within the ordinary 5-year reassessment period, extended to 10 years where tax evasion is suspected (Art. 42 VAT Act). If the mandatory documentation bundle is incomplete and export evidence is not produced within the accounting period (with the 180-day settlement benchmark applied to final payment evidence), the export exemption is retrospectively reversed, all related input VAT deductions are clawed back, and the VAT deficiency is assessed together with default interest at the ESTV-applicable rate (currently 3.5% per annum). Intentional evasion to obtain a fraudulent export zero-rating carries a fine of up to three times the tax evaded; negligent evasion carries a fine of up to one time the tax evaded (Art. 99 VAT Act); procedural violations such as non-compliant invoices or late registration are fined up to CHF 1,000 per offence (Art. 98 VAT Act). Export documents must be retained for 10 years (Art. 958f Swiss Code of Obligations); Swiss law does not formally require an inward remittance certificate, but payment and settlement evidence must be retained and the burden of proof shifts to the exporter where records are missing or inconsistent.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Swiss franc is fully convertible under both current and capital account headings as codified in the OECD Code of Liberalisation of Capital Movements and the IMF Article VIII. No exchange control restrictions apply to profit remittance, dividend distribution, or liquidation proceeds. Dividend remittances are, however, subject to a 35% Swiss withholding tax unless reduced under an applicable double taxation treaty, with the recipient being required to submit a tax residence certificate and Form 823 to obtain treaty benefits. Capital account convertibility is unrestricted for inward and outward investment, and there are no currency surrender or conversion mandates for non-resident shareholders.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Switzerland imposes no mandatory export proceeds surrender, repatriation timeline, or conversion ratio. Exporters are free to hold foreign currency receipts in domestic or offshore accounts without any SNB reporting requirement, apart from standard statistical balance-of-payments reporting applicable to transactions exceeding certain thresholds. Therefore, the statutory surrender ratio is 0% (not applicable) and there is no deadline for conversion into CHF.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-to-Low for offshore digital Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs). An offshore EMI not holding a Swiss banking licence or FINMA-recognised passport cannot lawfully operate as a payment institution in Switzerland or hold client funds in the form of Swiss e-money. For a Swiss AG processing marketplace settlements via Stripe or Etsy, the use of a regulated Payment Service Provider (PSP) under FINMA supervision is preferred. Offshore EMIs may support payout aggregation from marketplaces but present KYC/AML concentration risks and are not viable as a primary treasury rail for maintaining capital escrow funds. Legal constraints include article 1 of the Swiss Banking Act (BankG), requiring a licence for deposit-taking, and the absence of EU/EEA passporting rights for Swiss entities using an EMI domiciled outside Switzerland.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) are generally required to appear physically at the bank branch for corporate account opening, particularly when the beneficial owner is a non-Swiss resident. In practice, several high-tier Swiss banks permit a remote video-based identification procedure in accordance with FINMA Circular 2016/07, but this is conditional on provision of notarised and apostilled company documents, certified passport copies, and an interactive interview via encrypted video call. For an AG with a low-risk commercial profile (novelty enamel pin manufacturing), most banks will require at least one in-person meeting for the president of the board or the managing director, and will require the original certificates of incorporation, board minutes, and specimen signatures to be physically submitted.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficiary owner (UBO) is a non-resident/non-tax-resident individual with no independently verifiable tax identification number
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copies of valid passport, formal tax residence certificate from the country of residence, signed source-of-wealth declaration, professional CV and career timeline, reference letters from a regulated financial institution or professional advisor, and public sanctions/negative-news screening report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shareholder structure contains a trust, foundation, or another intermediation in a non-cooperative jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Measures-based legal opinion on the intermediary, complete organisational chart showing natural persons behind the trust/foundation, certified trust deed or foundation charter, declarations of political exposure, and a forensic accounting report on the provenance of subscribed capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected transaction profile involves high-frequency cross-border marketplace sales with low-ticket payment aggregation, raising potential customer-not-present risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed commercial business plan for die-struck brass enamel lapel pins, marketplace settlement statements from Etsy and Stripe, supply contracts with suppliers of brass and enamel materials, export customs declarations (e-EAD/CN22), estimated annual turnover and cash-flow projection, and a customer due diligence policy for online sales.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound shareholder loans and equity injections must comply with the Swiss anti-money laundering framework, which requires a bank to declare the origin of funds and to file a payment purpose form. A compliant routing uses SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR-denominated injections) with a clear reference to 'Kapitaleinlage' (Capital Contribution) or 'Aktionärsdarlehen' (Shareholder Loan). The underlying corporate documents must evidence the capital increase or loan agreement, together with a notarised board resolution and, if applicable, the commercial register notification. Since Switzerland has no exchange controls, no central bank approval or foreign investment notification is required, but the recipient bank may request a 'Bekanntgabe der wirtschaftlichen Begünstigten' (UBO disclosure form) and a contract proving the commercial reason for the transfer.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements related to raw material sourcing of brass, enamel, and packaging, the beneficiary suppliers can be paid via SWIFT MT103 in the supplier's currency; for EU suppliers, EUR SEPA Credit Transfers are the preferred low-cost rail. Higher-value and more complex shipments support the use of commercial letters of credit (documentary credits governed by ICC UCP 600), with issuing bank guaranteeing payment against presentation of commercial invoice, bill of lading/airway bill, packing list, certificate of origin, and quality inspection certificate. Domestic CHF payments are cleared via SIC (Swiss Interbank Clearing) in real time. For payroll, social security contributions, and VAT remittances, direct-debit (LSV+ / DD) rails are accepted.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla FX forwards (delivery-based) with offshore or onshore Swiss counterparties
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in restricted or soft currencies when the commercial invoice value is linked to an emerging-market currency
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) to swap the CHF capital contribution into USD/EUR operating liquidity for input procurement
Over-the-counter FX options (calls and puts) for asymmetric protection on accounts receivable from Etsy and Stripe
Plain-vanilla interest-rate swaps (only if debt is syndicated or refinanced in multiple currencies)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income and capital tax return (direct federal, cantonal and municipal taxes) accompanied by annual financial statements per Art. 958e CO
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration (collects Direct Federal Tax on behalf of ESTV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year AG: filed by 31 March – 30 April following fiscal year-end; extension to 30 September available through accredited tax agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest 3.5%–4.5% p.a.; procedural fines up to CHF 8,000; surcharge up to 40% of evaded tax; criminal prosecution for deliberate false statements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT return (annual, quarterly or monthly method) covering worldwide taxable turnover; annual filing available when net turnover ≤ CHF 500,000
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: ESTV – Swiss Federal Tax Administration, VAT Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 60 days after end of each reporting period; annual declaration due by 1 March for a 31 December year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Arrears interest 4.5% p.a.; administrative fines up to CHF 8,000; 10%–40% surcharge on unpaid VAT; enforced collection proceedings upon continued default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting: minutes, approval of annual accounts, profit appropriation and discharge of the Board, coupled with reconciliation of share register and beneficial owner register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company statutory records (share register and minutes book); Commercial Register notified only upon Board or auditor changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must be convened within 6 months of financial year-end (Art. 699 para. 1 CO)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Warning from Commercial Register Office under Art. 731b CO; if unresolved, court-ordered dissolution of the corporation; directors face joint liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Register notifications for annual corporate changes (re-election of directors or auditor, changes in registered office, capital measures and UBO-relevant organic modifications)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt), with SHAB publication
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after each registrable event; no annual standing filing required if no organic change, but register record must remain accurate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to CHF 5,000 (Art. 943 CO); false declarations prosecuted under Art. 952a CO; strike-off with liquidation after unheeded Art. 731b CO warnings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary audit triggered when two of three thresholds are exceeded for two consecutive years: total assets > CHF 20 million; turnover > CHF 40 million; average > 250 full-time employees (Art. 727 CO). Otherwise limited audit required, unless waived by unanimous shareholder resolution where ≤ 10 FTE (opt-out, Art. 727a CO).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (Art. 957–963f CO) constituting Swiss GAAP; IFRS or Swiss GAAP FER optionally applied; commercial balance sheet adjusted for tax per DBG and StHG.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual internal UBO reconciliation performed at the AGM; register lists every natural person holding ≥25% of voting rights or capital (Art. 697j CO); updates must be made within 30 days of any share transfer or capital change; no public annual UBO filing exists in Switzerland, but authorities may demand access at any time.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficial Owners (UBO, Art. 697j CO)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,700 – 3,400 annually for domiciliation and administrative agent in rural cantons; central Zug/Zurich USD 2,300 – 6,800
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,300 – 7,900 for limited audit; USD 0 with valid opt-out; ordinary audit from USD 13,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% Swiss federal corporate income tax, plus cantonal and communal tax (combined effective rate approx. 11.9% in Canton Zug and approx. 21% in Canton Zurich)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays. Permanent preferential reliefs: participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains with a 5% non-deductible notional cost (Art. 69 DBG); patent box deduction of up to 90% on Swiss IP-derived income under certain cantons; R&D super-deduction of up to 150% (canton-dependent); notional interest deduction in Zurich and Geneva; tax loss carryforward of 7 years (Art. 67 DBG)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Combined cantonal and federal corporate tax return for legal entities (Zuger Steuererklärung für juristische Personen / Federal Tax Return for Juristic Persons), lodged electronically via the eTax Zug portal; federal direct tax assessed on the same return; VAT returns filed separately via the ESTV/AFC ePortal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Return due within 6 months after fiscal year-end; calendar-year AGs (31 December year-end) must file by 30 June of the following year unless an extension is granted by the cantonal tax administration

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross operating revenue (Erlös aus Lieferungen und Leistungen) exclusive of VAT
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report Swiss-source turnover from enamel pin sales (Etsy/Stripe payment rails) only; foreign branch income is exempt with progression under Art. 52 DBG upon submission of an allocation statement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses: cost of materials, subcontracting, wages, rent, logistics, sales commissions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only business-related expenses economically borne by the Swiss taxable unit are deductible; cross-border intercompany charges require contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Depreciation and amortization (Abschreibungen): tooling, dies, molds, plant and equipment
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use commercial depreciation rates consistent with actual useful life; no depreciation on hidden reserves created or funded by foreign shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provisions and accruals (Rückstellungen): warranty, returns, bad debts, inventory obsolescence
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Requirements: business justification, economic probability and arm's length accounting practice under Art. 63 DBG; unjustified provisions are reversed into taxable income.
Start from statutory annual accounts; add back non-deductible items such as excessive director remuneration, in-kind shareholder benefits, non-business expenses and unabsorbed withholding tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions and reliefs: participation deduction, patent box, R&D super-deduction, loss carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Available only where the Swiss AG holds qualifying substantial participations or performs qualifying R&D in Switzerland; supporting documentation in German, French or Italian is required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits: Swiss withholding tax credits and foreign tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders cannot credit Swiss withholding tax against personal taxes; relief occurs exclusively through the DTA refund procedure with the ESTV.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: procedural fine up to CHF 10,000 under Art. 174 DBG plus default interest on the assessed tax (approx. 3.5% per annum federal); incomplete or false returns triggering evasion proceedings expose fines up to the amount of the tax evaded and, for qualified fraud, imprisonment up to three years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on all dividends distributed by the AG; reduced to 0%-15% under applicable double tax treaties (e.g., 5% on dividends paid to a Chinese corporate shareholder holding at least 25% under the CH-CN DTA; 0% on substantial holdings under selected treaties)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Swiss paying AG must withhold 35% at distribution. The foreign shareholder must apply to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) for a refund within three years from the end of the calendar year in which the dividend became due, submitting: (i) the official tax residence certificate (TRC) of the shareholder's state of residence, (ii) a declaration of beneficial ownership and shareholding percentage, and (iii) dividend payment and bank documentation. If the paying agent is ESTV-approved, the reduced treaty rate may be applied at source under the simplified notification procedure. Refund rights lapse after the statutory period; shell entities without substantive ownership are denied relief.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% Swiss withholding tax on cross-border licensing payments generally; an exception applies to royalty payments for rights registered in a Swiss public register and exploited in Switzerland, which are subject to 35% WHT. Interest: 0% WHT on ordinary private intercompany loans; 35% WHT on bond interest and bank deposit interest. CH-CN DTA generally caps interest at 10% and royalties at 10%, subject to beneficial ownership and anti-abuse rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Swiss TP documentation duty (Art. 58a DBG and the Swiss TP Documentation Ordinance) applies where the Swiss entity's annual net revenue reaches CHF 80 million in two consecutive business years, or where material cross-border related-party transactions require contemporaneous records; multinational groups with consolidated revenue of CHF 900 million or more must file an OECD Country-by-Country report with the ESTV.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland applies a de facto economic substance requirement through the place-of-effective-management rule (Art. 50 DBG) and the prohibition on sham transactions (Art. 126 DBG): the enamel pin AG must maintain an office, personnel, Swiss bank accounts, board decisions, accounting records and commercial functions in Switzerland. Letterbox companies are denied treaty benefits and 35% dividend WHT relief, and their income may be re-attributed to the ultimate beneficial owner.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilful or grossly negligent omission of Swiss-source revenue from Etsy/Stripe sales, inflation of cost of goods sold, double deduction of input VAT, or fabrication of supplier invoices for enamel pin production
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Evasion: fine up to the amount of the evaded tax plus default interest under Art. 175 DBG; qualified tax fraud with falsified records: imprisonment up to three years and/or fine up to three times the evaded tax under Art. 186 DBG; additional cantonal fines in Zug
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false returns are criminally liable as perpetrators; civil restitution actions under Art. 754 CO for the company's tax damage; personal asset seizures and travel bans in mutual assistance proceedings

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Swiss AG as a pure mailbox with no operational premises, staff or management function in Switzerland, while claiming Swiss residence status, treaty refunds and 35% WHT exemption on outbound dividends
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of the sham structure under Art. 126 DBG; denial of tax residence status, DTA treaty relief and WHT refunds; 35% Verrechnungssteuer assessed on deemed distributions; retroactive taxation with default interest and administrative fines
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Veil-piercing for unpaid taxes and WHT amounts; directors personally liable for deficiencies realized in liquidation; criminal charges for obtaining treaty benefits by false declarations; possible disqualification from Swiss board positions

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating Etsy Direct Pay or Stripe merchant accounts without completing AML due diligence, failing to maintain beneficial ownership registers, or accepting third-party payments without identifying the payor
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Anti-Money Laundering Act (GwG/AMLA) administrative fines up to CHF 500,000; qualified money laundering under Art. 305bis Swiss Criminal Code: imprisonment up to five years and/or fine; forfeiture of illicit funds
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Director appointed as money-laundering reporting officer faces direct criminal liability; personal fines and imprisonment; civil compensation to the company for reputational and regulatory losses

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling enamel pins to a related foreign distributor below arm's length, paying excessive royalties to a related IP holder, or funding the AG via disproportionate related-party debt (thin capitalization above the 3:1 debt-to-equity safe harbor)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Upward tax reassessment to the arm's length profit; disallowance of excess royalty and interest deductions; recharacterization of excess payments as constructive dividends subject to 35% WHT; TP documentation fines up to CHF 10,000 per offence
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Joint and several liability of approving directors for reassessed taxes under Art. 754 CO; criminal exposure for aiding tax evasion; freezing orders on personal assets in aggravated cases
